paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: forgiveness and love go together, and Jesus says so Himself. He tells Simon a story about two men who couldn't pay, and the moneylender forgave both of them (Luke 7:41-42). Then He says, "her many sins have been forgiven, for she has loved much. But he who has been forgiven little loves little." (Luke 7:47). Her love wasn't the price she paid. It was what showed up after she had been forgiven.

Now watch what that does to us. Simon was so busy reviewing the woman that he never looked at his own account. I know that little voice, friend. It's LOUD, and it never reviews ITSELF. Whoever you are, you owe a debt you can't pay, and the moneylender in the story shows what Jesus does with a debt like that.

Jesus doesn't stop at the story. He tells the woman, "Your sins are forgiven," and then, "Your faith has saved you; go in peace." (Luke 7:48, 50). Right after that, the passage shows women who had been healed traveling with Jesus and ministering "out of their own means." (Luke 8:2-3). That's what a forgiven heart looks like, friend: it gives, it follows and it goes in peace. I know what it feels like to be pulled out of the dark, and I bake with a thankful heart every day because of it.
